result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers take a clear position and address the setup burden directly, with guided or concierge setup. A goes further: it agrees on a written success test with named owners and a day-14 review, and it uses a qualification gate (felt problem, signer, willingness to share schedules) to separate serious prospects from those gathering options. Neither answer gives the actual wording for replying to 'can we try it for free', though A at least offers to draft it. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a conditional trial and see the day of setup as the real cost, and both fix it by doing the setup for the clinic. B is stronger because it adds a qualification check (how much pain they feel now, who signs off, whether they'll give the setup time), a success test agreed in writing, a day-14 checkpoint and a named owner on each side; A defines success but never sets a joint review date or says who decides. Neither answer gives the actual reply to send a prospect, though B at least offers to write one.
